title: Pilot Seeding Sprint: Compact Battlecard Workbench (Draft)
content:
NOT FOR CUSTOMER SHARE — compact internal workbench for sellers running short pilot conversations.

Purpose:
- Provide a 1–2 page, super-skim battlecard for quick prep before a pilot kickoff or SDR handoff.
- Emphasis: rapid qualification hooks, fallback economics, and the single most convincing evidence points for platform engineers and product owners.

Audience:
- SEs, SDRs running qualification calls, seller handling platform-engineer POCs, AE prepping a pilot kick.

One-liner to use (30s):
- "Redwood gives you predictable inference latency and unit economics across hosted, reserved, and private deployments—so you can ship LLM features without building and operating a custom serving stack."

Top 5 value bullets (for the engineer):
1) Predictable latency SLOs across 99p tail with routing fallbacks (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private).
2) Up to 3x token-cost reduction on stateful workloads via prefix & KV caching + batching.
3) Transparent per-token costing and token-level traces for debugging regressions.
4) Rapid canary and A/B rollouts + automated fallback policies to keep features live during capacity events.
5) Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem) with KMS/HSM and audit logs for regulated data.

60-second demo path (script bullets):
- Start with a single prompt that represents the customer’s heavy path (e.g., 3-turn customer support flow).
- Show token-level latency on Console, then flip to same flow with prefix-caching enabled (show token cost drop).
- Trigger a canary rollback and show how traffic splits and fallback preserves latency.
- End with quick note: Dedicated reserve sizing recommendation and TCO sketch.

Top technical signals (yes/no checklist for pilot fit):
- Is the workload latency-sensitive at 100–500ms P50 and <1s P95? -> YES: emphasize routing & Dedicated.
- Are you doing stateful multi-turn chat with long context? -> YES: highlight KV caching and cost wins.
- Does security/regulation require customer-managed KMS or air-gap? -> YES: lean Private deployment.
- Is customer volume seasonally spiky with sustained baseline? -> YES: propose Dedicated + autoscale + burst.

Objections and tight rebut scripts (quick):
- "We can self-host and save money": 
  - Rebut: "Totally reasonable for large scale. Most teams underestimate ops cost and latency debugging headroom—we provide a predictable ops surface + kernel-level optimizations tuned to LLM patterns. If you want, we can run a 2-week pilot that compares your self-host baseline with Redwood’s Dedicated profile (same model) so you can see real latency and unit-cost deltas."
- "We need model control / custom weights":
  - Rebut: "We support model pinning, and our Dedicated/Private paths let you bring custom weights while keeping our runtime benefits (KV cache, batching). We also run a compatibility validation during onboarding to surface performance regressions."
- "Price seems high for pilot":
  - Rebut: "We usually structure pilots with capped committed hours + discount and show a 3–5x development speedup (reduced infra ops). We can model TCO over 90 days for your expected traffic."

Evidence & quick metrics (put on slide if asked):
- Typical latency baseline: P50 70–100ms, P95 300–600ms (hosted profiles for 8k context family).
- KV/prefix caching win: 20–60% token cost reduction in multi-turn support flows (customer references available).
- Batch savings: 1.5–2x throughput improvement on mixed short/long prompt workloads.
- SLA uptime options: Hosted (99.9%), Dedicated (99.95), Private SLA negotiable.

Competitive differentiators to call out (concise):
- Versus managed cloud endpoints: We bundle the runtime kernel optimizations + routing policies out-of-the-box; fewer perf surprises.
- Versus LLM APIs: Better pick-your-deployment model + clearer TCO controls across caching/quantization.
- Versus open-source runtimes: You keep the same developer API across hosted/dedicated/private and get production-grade fallbacks and tracing.

When to propose what (decision heuristics):
- Hosted-first: quick POC, low-risk, low-commitment teams; fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput, enterprise accounts with steady traffic or latency SLOs.
- Private: regulated workloads, customer-managed KMS, on-prem constraints.

Pilot offer structure (recommended):
- 30-day rapid pilot: capped consumption + 2 SE checkpoints (kickoff, mid-pilot perf review) + final TCO/rollout recommendations.
- Data we collect: latency profiles, token-level costs, model variant regressions, error rates.

Demo & handoff checklist (quick for SE):
- Pre-call: confirm primary flow + sample prompts, expected QPS, retention window for KV cache.
- Kickoff: run baseline trace, enable caching, measure delta, confirm SLA expectation.
- Mid-pilot: share Console snapshot + one regression alert example.
- Close: TCO sheet + recommended commit level for Dedicated or plan for Private.

Script snippets sellers can paste into email (short):
- Subject: Quick pilot: lower latency + predictable per-token costs
- Body: "Hi {name}, could we run a 30-day pilot to compare your current inference stack against Redwood? We’ll instrument one representative flow, show latency and cost deltas, and come away with a clear recommendation (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). No long-term lock-in for the pilot."

Open questions / risks to resolve before next sync:
- Customer expected P95 SLA requirement (explicit number) — owner: Mateo.
- If proposing Private, confirm KMS vendor and on-prem network constraints — owner: Priya.
- Need model family and quantization tolerance (which models can we run w/ higher perf kernels) — owner: Owen.

Quick wins to add to the deck before seller enablement session:
- Add a 1-row TCO example for a 1M token/month e-commerce chat workload (approx numbers).
- Insert a short customer quote (ops lead) about rollback + canary preserving uptime.
- Add link to quick-run Jupyter that SEs can use during pilot kickoff (internal repo link in linked_artifacts).

Next steps (owners):
- Draft 1-page PDF battlecard for seller Slack pin — Lena (due 2025-02-24).
- Run one dry demo with SE team and capture console screenshots — Owen (due 2025-02-20).
- Validate TCO sheet numbers with finance (small-scope) — Mateo (due 2025-02-25).

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Keep language simple; goal is to reduce prep time for SEs to <10 minutes.
- Consider a micro-template for pilots that auto-populates from Console metrics (follow-up ask for product ops).

References / quick links:
- CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-SEED-2034 (pilot templates)
- JIRA-PLT-1221 (pilot instrumentation ticket)
- internal demo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/458

— end of workbench draft —

Unresolved: how to present quantization tradeoffs succinctly on a single slide without diving into phonetic details — maybe a simple 3-cell table (accuracy, latency, price) with typical ranges.
